content:
The image shows a mango leaf with:
- Whitish-gray powdery patches scattered across the upper leaf surface
- Patches are irregular, dusty/flour-like in texture
- No necrotic lesions with defined margins (rules out Anthracnose)
- No dark sooty coating covering the surface uniformly (rules out Sooty Mould)
- No tip/branch dieback (rules out Die_Back)
- The white powdery residue is characteristic of fungal mycelium and conidia on the leaf surface

This matches Powdery Mildew, caused by *Oidium mangiferae*, which produces exactly this kind of pale gray-white powdery coating on mango leaves.
